agent_priors_used: General prior (not SPIDER evidence): research agents exhibit path dependence and local-attractor behavior, so an inherited next_question can be locally rational yet globally suboptimal and a cognitive reset is warranted before continuing a flagged lane.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): a treatment cannot be shown to beat a comparator that already sits at the correctness ceiling, so dynamic range / non-degeneracy must be certified arithmetically before any expensive multi-arm comparison is funded.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): a prerequisite observed failing identically across lanes should be repaired once at the substrate/control-plane level, not rediscovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID/design-failure in each lane.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): serial gating chains make off-path breadth cheap but not free; critical-path lanes should be concentrated and off-path lanes pointed at the highest-value non-gated question or parked, each with an explicit park branch.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): cache/memory invalidation is harder than population and un-questioned stale knowledge is a correctness hazard, so false-accept-first freshness and repair metrics matter more than coverage.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): small CPU-quantized language models frequently cannot emit reliable structured actions for multi-step tool/Web use, so endpoint capability must be validated against the actual task before an expensive four-arm benchmark is authorized.
General prior (not SPIDER evidence): shipping verified code through a pinned promotion path rather than copying experiment code prevents drift between the audited carrier and the production kernel.
